requirements.description: Every requirement of a delivery exists in a versioned matrix before implementation.
A Test Rework / Green Keeper role forbids shipping anything red and records every cycle.
A Delivery Completeness Validator audits the matrix before handoff and may not implement.
`GREEN_KEEPER_GATE` and `DELIVERY_COMPLETENESS_GATE` are preconditions of `READY_FOR_REVIEW`.
Readiness and blockage can never be claimed together.
Every operation attempt is recorded, including a refusal decided before execution.
Every recorded command is reproducible from its declared working directory.
The mandatory delivery order is stated in full in every governing document and both adapters.
The project keeps an organizational engineering memory of confirmed failures.
A lesson is `GUARDED` only when an automated control prevents recurrence.
A repeat increments recurrence, and a repeat against a guardrail is a `GUARDRAIL_FAILURE`.
A mandatory preflight selects the lessons that constrain each Gate.
Applicable lessons become requirements whose absence blocks completeness.
Lesson candidates can be extracted from recorded delivery evidence, never above `OBSERVED`.
requirements.evidence: Candidates recorded in this checkpoint's evidence.

requirements.description: External validation is grouped into milestones `M0` to `M6`.
An internal verdict is never described as independent external validation.
An extraordinary audit requires a recorded trigger.
Every completed Gate produces a retrospective.
One promotion invariant governs every positive terminal status, not only `READY_FOR_REVIEW`.
The mandatory quality gate set is a closed machine-readable registry that an invocation cannot narrow.
The expected requirement set is derived from canonical sources and compared exactly with the declared set.
An external milestone PASS is derived from an audit attestation authored by another sealed checkpoint.
A derived artifact carries a fingerprint of its inputs, and staleness is decided by recomputation.
Every lesson control, evidence path and provenance locator is resolved against the repository.
Every `GUARDED` lesson names a registered guardrail, and guardrail effectiveness is measured.
Sealed checkpoints are anchored by a hash-linked chain over tag, commit and tree.
Every count used as evidence is derived once and verified wherever a report states it.
Sealing is monotonic and post-commit, and every recorded command binds its declared inputs by content.
A milestone delivery carries an internal Red Team and an internal mirror audit, and neither is recorded as external validation.
Every finding of an independent audit is closed before the corrective delivery is offered.
A milestone verdict is carried by the audit checkpoint about a sealed subject, and its positive path is executed rather than only its refusals.
A generic guardrail derives repository state instead of naming a historical checkpoint, and the protocol's own next steps keep every mandatory gate green.
Every adversarial battery records a null-mutation control, and no count used as evidence is stated in prose.

An audit control tells an empty applicable set from a missing required set, justifies every `NOT_APPLICABLE` against a canonical derivation no delivery can shrink, and a simulation that claims a control passed executes that control instead of writing its artifact.
An independent review is recorded.
An adversarial Red Team is recorded.
`GATE_PASS` is granted only by a run independent of the implementer.
requirements.evidence: The implementing run closes at `READY_FOR_REVIEW`; the validator refuses `GATE_PASS` without a passed or explicitly waived cross-tool validation.

requirements.description: Every test suite this Gate introduces is declared canonically and is counted by the count derivation and resolvable as evidence.
The internal mirror audit judges the Gate it runs in rather than a Gate named in its own source.
The internal Red Team battery of this Gate is executable, scoped to the Foundation, and records a null-mutation control.
The repository carries the planned application, service, package and infrastructure directories.
A directory reserved for a later Gate says so and contains no implementation.
No later-Gate capability is implemented, simulated or faked in this Gate.
The backend is a real FastAPI application that starts reliably and fails loudly when it cannot.
Shutdown is graceful and releases every client the application opened.
Dependency lifecycle is explicit and held on the application, not in ambient mutable globals.
`GET /health` reports process liveness and does not depend on external dependencies to answer.
`GET /ready` probes PostgreSQL, Redis, MinIO and Temporal and refuses readiness when a mandatory dependency is unavailable.
`GET /version` reports the application version and build identity and exposes no secret.
The application exposes a Prometheus metrics endpoint with request, latency, status and dependency metrics.
OpenAPI documentation describes the Foundation endpoints and exposes no internal-only route.
CORS is configured explicitly from configuration, without a permissive wildcard, and allows the local frontend.
Configuration is typed, validated at load time and rejects an invalid or missing mandatory value.
Safe defaults, development configuration and test configuration are separated rather than conflated.
A committed example environment file documents every key and carries no real secret, and the real file is ignored by Git.
Secret values are redacted wherever configuration, errors or logs could expose them.
No secret is baked into an image, a compose file, a Dockerfile or a committed configuration file.
PostgreSQL runs locally from the compose stack at a pinned version with a persistent named volume.
The persistence layer is real, asynchronous and pooled, built on SQLAlchemy 2.
Alembic migrations run from zero against an empty database and produce the declared schema.
Starting against an already-migrated database neither fails nor recreates the schema.
A failed migration never produces a healthy readiness or a silent partial start.
The structural domain tables the later Gates build on exist, with their relationships and constraints.
Identifiers use one consistent strategy, UUIDv7, implemented and tested rather than assumed.
The common column convention is defined once and applied where it makes sense, not forced everywhere.
The pgvector position is decided, recorded, and — where the extension is enabled — migrated and tested.
Redis runs locally from the compose stack at a pinned version.
The backend holds a real Redis client whose availability the readiness probe verifies.
An integration test exercises a real Redis round trip against the running service.
MinIO runs locally from the compose stack at a pinned version with a persistent named volume.
The buckets the later Gates need are created by an idempotent bootstrap that is safe to re-run.
The readiness probe verifies real object-storage connectivity rather than a reachable port.
An integration test writes, reads and deletes a real object.
Temporal runs locally from the compose stack at a pinned version with its persistent state.
An IACode worker connects to Temporal and polls its task queue as a first-class service.
The readiness probe verifies real Temporal connectivity.
A minimal real workflow and activity execute end to end through the worker and return an observable result.
No agent workflow, tool call or orchestration of a later Gate is implemented here.
A real Angular application exists and builds reproducibly with pinned dependencies.
The Foundation page identifies IACode and renders the live backend health, readiness and version.

requirements.description: The API base address is centralized in configuration, carries no secret and is not hardcoded across the code.
Frontend unit tests run headless and are part of the verification command.
Every image builds from a pinned base, runs as a non-root user where practical, carries no secret and excludes build waste.
The compose stack declares every Foundation service and nothing that the Foundation does not need.
Every service that can report health has a real healthcheck, and start-up ordering uses those conditions instead of fixed sleeps.
Restart behaviour is declared, and the stack recovers its state after a restart.
Durable state lives in named volumes that are documented, not in the container filesystem.
The stack uses an explicit network and publishes only the ports local development needs, from configuration.
The backend and the worker emit structured logs carrying the contract fields, absent rather than invented when there is no context.
Every HTTP request carries a correlation identifier that is accepted or generated, propagated, returned and logged.
The API error contract is explicit, extensible and never returns a traceback or internal detail to the client while keeping it in the logs.
Prometheus is provisioned and scrapes the API and the worker.
Grafana starts with the Prometheus datasource and a Foundation dashboard provisioned automatically.
The OpenTelemetry position for the Foundation is decided and recorded rather than left implicit.
A reproducible backup produces a PostgreSQL dump and the object-storage contents, with a correct exit code and a log, and fails loudly on partial failure.
The backup never writes a credential into its artifacts or its log.
A restore reconstructs the database and the object storage from a backup produced by this tooling.
Backup and restore are verified end to end with synthetic data in a disposable environment, and the restored data is checked rather than assumed.
Backup retention for the Foundation is either implemented simply or documented as out of scope, with no silent gap.
One documented command runs the whole Gate verification and works on the primary Windows environment as well as on POSIX.
The backend suite covers health, readiness, version, configuration, redaction, error handling, correlation, database, cache, object storage, workflows and migrations.
The frontend suite covers bootstrap, the status rendering and the API configuration, and the production build succeeds.
Infrastructure smoke validation proves that our own configuration of each service is operational.
A fresh installation with no previous volume reaches a ready stack, a migrated database, a reachable frontend and a green smoke check.
A restart of the running stack returns every service to ready with its data intact.
With a mandatory dependency stopped, liveness may stay up while readiness fails correctly, and readiness recovers when the dependency returns.
Lint and static analysis run over the backend, the worker and the frontend and are green.
A dependency vulnerability scan is executed, or its absence is justified, and relevant Critical and High findings block the Gate.

requirements.description: Every structural decision of this Gate that is not already recorded becomes an ADR, and no ADR duplicates an existing decision.

requirements.description: Every test suite this Gate introduces is declared canonically, is counted by the count derivation and is resolvable as evidence.
The internal Red Team battery of this Gate is executable, scoped to the Model Gateway, and records a null-mutation control.
The reservation of the gateway directory is consumed by the Gate that owns it, and the scope registry keeps constraining every path still owned by a later Gate.
One documented command verifies this Gate, adds the stages it introduces and keeps a targeted mode that does not restart the stack.
The Model Gateway lives in the directory the Foundation reserved for it and is consumed in process, and the boundary decision is recorded rather than implied.
No consumer outside the adapter layer names a provider-specific endpoint, payload field or product name.
The gateway declares its persistence and clock ports and imports no application module, so the dependency points inward.
No later-Gate capability — tool execution, agent lifecycle, sandboxing, retrieval, experience storage or training — is implemented, simulated or faked here.
The gateway directory stops declaring itself reserved and describes what this Gate delivered.

A canonical request carries correlation, messages, routing intent, required capabilities, sampling, output limits, streaming intent, tools, structured output and metadata, and is validated when it is built.
The message contract expresses the system, developer, user, assistant and tool roles independently of any provider's vocabulary.
The canonical response normalizes content, tool calls, finish reason, usage, latency, provider, model, endpoint, route and fallback chain, and the raw provider payload is never the public contract.
Tool definitions and tool calls are normalized into internal types with identifier, name and arguments, and the gateway executes no tool.
A tool call whose arguments are not valid JSON produces a normalized error instead of a partially parsed call.
Structured output is requested only from a model whose capability is known, and a request that needs it is refused or routed elsewhere rather than sent hopefully.
The contract carries an explicit version, so a consumer can detect an incompatible change instead of discovering one.
A provider contract declares health, model discovery, generation and streaming, and is not shaped by any one provider.
An OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions adapter builds the request, parses the response, parses the stream and maps the error.
An OpenAI-compatible Responses adapter builds the request, parses the response, parses the stream and maps the error.
An Anthropic-compatible Messages adapter builds the request, parses the response, parses the stream and maps the error.
The protocol is selected from the capabilities and endpoints the catalog records, the shape of the request and the provider configuration, never assumed from a default path.
A request that needs an endpoint the model does not declare is refused before it reaches the network.
No fictitious provider is registered in the runtime configuration; the deterministic double exists only inside the test fixtures.

Provider configuration is versionable and carries no credential value: an identifier, an adapter, an enabled flag, a base URL reference, the name of the secret variable, the discovery endpoint and the protocols supported.
The provider registry persists operational metadata — adapter, enabled state, health, last check and catalog state — and never a credential.
A credential is resolved from the environment at call time and reaches no database row, response body, log record, metric label or catalog record.
Every configuration key this Gate declares is read by the implementation.
A provider base URL is validated: HTTPS for a remote provider, plain HTTP only for a loopback address, and never user information embedded in the URL.
A provider address can never be supplied by an inference request; it comes from administrative configuration alone.
The catalog is discovered from the provider API, and no list written by hand is treated as authoritative.

A normalized model record carries the provider model identifier, display name, family, context window, maximum output tokens, supported endpoints, streaming, vision, tools, structured output, reasoning levels, active state, raw metadata and the synchronization instant.
An absent capability stays unknown and is never normalized into a negative answer.
Every capability records where it came from: provider metadata, manual configuration or observation, and never inference from a model's name.
Synchronization is idempotent: running it twice over the same provider answer changes nothing the second time.
A model that disappears from the provider answer is deactivated rather than destroyed, so the calls recorded against it stay readable.
A partial, invalid or failed synchronization leaves the previous catalog usable: the answer is validated and normalized before anything is committed.
Model identity is the provider together with the provider's own model identifier, so two providers exposing the same name do not collide.
Routing reads normalized fields; the raw provider metadata is kept for diagnosis and is never the thing a decision depends on.
The router is deterministic and applies a documented order: validate, explicit override, candidates, capability filter, context filter, route policy, configured priority, execution, fallback.
An explicit model is honored when the policy allows it and is refused, rather than silently replaced, when it cannot serve the request.
A default model is configurable, and a request with no model and no usable default fails with a clear error instead of an arbitrary choice.
Required capabilities eliminate candidates that cannot satisfy them, and an unknown capability is refused unless the policy explicitly allows it.
The gateway never knowingly sends a request larger than the context window it knows about, and an estimated token count is labelled an estimate rather than reported as exact.
A reasoning effort is validated against the levels the model or the provider declares, and an incompatible level produces a fallback or an explicit error rather than a silent send.
Route aliases are configuration, not built-in preference, and the system claims no empirical superiority for any of them.
No model quality score, benchmark result or comparative claim is invented anywhere in this Gate.
Every routing result carries a short structured explanation of the decision, and never a model's private reasoning.
A disabled provider and an inactive model are never selected.

An internal error taxonomy distinguishes authentication, authorization, rate limiting, unknown model, invalid request, context limit, provider unavailability, provider timeout, transient and permanent provider failure, an open circuit, cancellation and an internal gateway failure, and every adapter maps onto it.
Timeouts are configurable, connect and read are separated, and no provider call can hang without bound.
A retry happens only for an error class a retry can resolve, and never for authentication, authorization, an invalid request, an unknown model, an invalid schema or a context limit.
A provider's `Retry-After` is honored within a configured bound, and an unreasonably long wait is refused rather than obeyed.
Backoff is exponential with jitter, and the test suite controls time instead of waiting for it.
A circuit breaker moves between closed, open and half-open per provider and per provider and model, from external configuration.
The fallback chain is bounded, never repeats a candidate, cannot loop, and the chain that was used is recorded.
Fallback happens only for the error classes another candidate could resolve, and an invalid request is not retried against a second model.
A consumer that cancels interrupts the upstream call and the attempt is recorded as cancelled.
Request limits are configurable and enforced: payload size, message count, tool count, output tokens and fallback depth.
A provider response larger than the configured bound is refused instead of being read into memory without limit.
An unavailable provider never makes the Foundation liveness endpoint fail; it is visible in the gateway's own health instead.
Streaming goes through the same router and the same adapter abstraction as a non-streaming call, with no parallel architecture.
Stream events are normalized into an envelope covering start, text delta, tool-call delta, usage, end and error.
Automatic fallback is allowed only before the first content reaches the consumer; after it, the error is propagated and no second model continues the stream.
A stream that fails after content ends with an explicit error event carrying the partial result, not with a silent completion.
The API streams over Server-Sent Events and stops the upstream call when the client disconnects.
Usage is normalized where the provider supplies it — input, output, total, cached and reasoning tokens — and a field the provider did not supply stays absent rather than being invented.
Cost is absent unless pricing is configured, and zero is never used to mean unknown.
Every attempt is recorded with its operational metadata: correlation, provider, model, endpoint, route, status, timestamps, latency, tokens, error type, retries and fallbacks.
Prompts, messages and completions are not persisted by default; the debug capture is opt-in, redacted, documented and off in every shipped configuration.
A request fingerprint may be stored for correlation, and its documentation states that a hash is not anonymization.
No provider reasoning content is stored; only the reasoning token count a provider reports.
Nothing this Gate persists becomes training data: the rights defaults of the provenance policy are preserved.
The gateway exposes request, duration, error, retry, fallback, circuit state, provider health and catalog size metrics through the existing Prometheus endpoint.
requirements.evidence: `GatewayMetricsTests`; Prometheus scrape after the live smoke.

requirements.description: No metric label carries a prompt, a completion, a credential or an unbounded value.
Structured logs carry the correlation and request identifiers, the provider, the model, the route, the attempt, the fallback index, the latency, the status and the error type where each is known.
An authorization header, an API key, a full prompt and a full response are never written to a log.
A correlation identifier propagates from the HTTP request through every provider attempt to the persisted record, so one call is traceable end to end.
The gateway API is versioned and documented in the OpenAPI document.
The provider listing returns safe metadata only and never a credential, an authorization header or a secret value.
The model listing filters by provider, by active state and by capability.
The synchronization endpoint reports what was added, updated, deactivated, unchanged and what failed, without exposing a provider secret.
The inference endpoint returns the normalized response, the route information, the usage and the request identifier, and never a stack trace.
The gateway health endpoint separates the process from the external provider, so an unreachable provider is reported without claiming the service is down.
A Model Gateway page shows the provider status, the model count, the last synchronization and the model list with its capabilities.

requirements.description: A minimal playground sends a prompt with a route or a model and an optional reasoning effort, and shows the chosen model, the provider, the answer, the latency and the usage when it exists.
No provider credential reaches the browser: the page calls the IACode backend and nothing else.
No conversation persistence, chat history, persona, agent interface or tool execution is added to the frontend.
The frontend suite covers the new page and its service, runs headless and is part of the verification command.
A real catalog synchronization runs against the configured provider API, parses the answer, normalizes it, persists it and repeats without changing anything.
A real non-streaming inference against the explicitly configured smoke model returns the expected text through the normalized response.
A real streaming inference produces a start, at least one delta and an end, with no duplicated content.
The configured smoke model is never silently substituted: its absence from the discovered catalog fails the check.
The live checks are minimal: a short prompt, a small output cap, no repetition, no deliberate rate limiting and no repeated authentication failure against the real provider.
The live inference produced a persisted record carrying the provider, the model, the status, the latency and the usage the provider supplied, and carrying no prompt.
The observability stack observed the live gateway request.

requirements.description: Without a configured provider credential the live validation fails loudly and the Gate is blocked, and no result is claimed that was not executed.
A provider contract suite proves discovery, generation, streaming, usage, error normalization, timeout, cancellation and tool-call normalization for every adapter.
The catalog suite covers a new model, changed metadata, a removed model, a duplicate, invalid metadata, an unknown capability, a failed transaction and a repeated synchronization.

The routing suite covers an explicit model, the default model, capability filtering, an unknown required capability, a disabled provider, an inactive model, an insufficient context window, route priority, fallback order and fallback exhaustion.
The retry suite proves which classes are retried — rate limiting, server failure, timeout, connection reset — and which are not: authentication, invalid request and context limit.
The circuit breaker suite covers the threshold, the open state, fast failure, the cooldown, the half-open probe, recovery and reopening, without waiting in real time.
The streaming suite covers a normal stream, an empty stream, a failure before the first delta, a failure after the first delta, consumer cancellation, usage at the end and a tool-call delta.
A test proves that two models' output can never be concatenated into one stream.
The structured-output suite proves that an incapable candidate is rejected and that a capable one receives the right configuration.
The secret suite proves that a credential appears in no log, no exception, no HTTP response, no persisted record, no metric and no catalog metadata.
Provider unavailability, an invalid credential and rate limiting are exercised with fixtures rather than against the real provider.
The deterministic provider double exists only under the test fixtures and cannot be reached from a runtime path.
The schema change of this Gate is a new migration, and no migration of the previous Gate is edited.
Every migration runs from zero against an empty database and produces the declared schema.
A database created by the previous Gate upgrades without loss.
